interactions.title: Wellby’s unread hobgoblin logbook
lines: Wellby: ((Barracks report))I found hobgoblin money, I think, and I pull out a handful of small silver discs stamped with the Blackened Claw mark. And silver and copper. Oh, and I found this too. I pull up a book. I think it’s a logbook. I think it’s hobgoblin, but I don’t read it. Do any of us know hobgoblin?

Wellby: When I look at it—so I open it up and I show you—there the short entries, at the top of which there are some like small, sort of repeating words. So I, I think these are dates. I think these are like date entries, if any of us happened to speak—
Kenzo: Nope.((Language-choice aside))I don’t think Kenzo would speak hobgoblin((Language-choice aside))
Seeker: So anything else we can determine from the log book? For example, does it end in an entry that trails off with a written scream? You—
DM: Know, because real people don’t write as they are being killed.
Seeker: Oh no, yeah. Does it descend into insanity, for instance? Or—
DM: No. Just kind of flipping through and you know, it does seem to have a series of dates, if the—if the words on the top of each entry are like a month in a year. And based on the frequency.
DM: Words change, it’s probably, probably something like three year—three years of entries that it represents. But it doesn’t end in a you know trail of blood or—
Delwath: Is it full, or does it end partway through the book?
DM: It ends partway through the book.

before: Seeker: Scratching and sniffing at the wall. And a rock and licking it occasionally.

DM: Yes, I’m sorry. So yes, interestingly enough, this seems to be something that was—it’s definitely—it seems like it’s been excavated more recently than than the main dwarven area, possibly within the last hundred to 200 years. It doesn’t have the sort of ancient feel that the dwarven outpost does, in terms of the, the sort of age of the construction and the age—I mean, things, things don’t weather fast in small underground areas, but this definitely seems—this tunnel definitely seems newer. Make a—make a Intelligence check. Okay, so do you also realize, as you’re walking past, that you did pass through an area at the sort of lowest point of the tunnel where the geology sort of shifted a little bit, like you’re passing, I guess not the lowest point in the tunnel—about three quarters of the way through the tunnel—where you’re passing from what was sort of loose sandstone—or not sandstone, limestone—to harder, harder rock. And as you’re standing kind of around the rope that Riswynn dropped, Wellby comes creeping up the tunnel.
Kenzo: What is—
Wellby: I did go back down over some of the ground that we covered, and also got a look out into the valley, which I think is over us right now. How are things here? We’re going up, apparently.
Seeker: Found some kind of cavern up there. Seems safe enough.
after: Kenzo: Oh, wait. Wait, I just—let’s, let’s try to piece this all together, going back a little bit if you don’t mind. So at the time of the Great War, what was happening here, 200 years ago?
DM: Who has a history proficiency?
Kenzo: I mean, I think I might kind of know some stuff.
Seeker: I think I do. Yeah, I do.
DM: Okay, so Kenzo and Seeker, give me a history.

interactions.title: Wellby reports a bat-like watcher
lines: Wellby: Well, I’ll tell you what I saw.((Lookout description))And I could see there was three of those humanoid hyenas. And they were driving a pack of wild dogs toward the gates, like herding them. Like shepherding them into the gates of Raven’s Hold. And stranger, though, way up high, there’s something watching them, following their progress, overseeing it maybe: this bat-like thing with a demony sort of body and long claws and spiky back, and it was unpleasant.
Wellby: So that was high up in flight over the plain. Well, the gnolls were herding these dogs toward the gates.
Wellby: On enormous bat wings. It’s just nice and regular size bat wings.
DM: It looked—at your first glance, it looks like just, you know, a slightly oversized bat, but then you pulled out your spyglass and you’re like—and you saw these other features.
Wellby: Oh, so it wasn’t just distance that made it look small?
DM: It was like really was.
DM: Without your spyglass, you would not have been able to tell about it wasn’t just the bat.
Kenzo: So was this alone, this beast that you saw it was, it didn’t seem intelligent? Was it—you felt like that was the master that it had other masters?

Wellby: It’s a good question, and I can’t properly say. Intelligent in the sense that it seemed like it was watching. I mean, this wasn’t just a you know buzzard circling. It was clearly watching and tracking their progress, but whether it was a reporter or a master, I—
Seeker: Were they watching it? So you guys—

DM: Ah, it’s hard to say. I mean, not that they were—you can’t tell whether they were aware of it. They were currently focused on driving a pack of wild dogs. They weren’t like glancing up every minute that check on that.

before: Wellby: You think they’re within the last century.
DM: Ah, one—within the last one—I mean, your memory, Wellby, was you know hundred, hundred 50 years ago. But that doesn’t necessarily mean that the, the hobgoblin clan itself is not older.
Wellby: Yeah, the, um, the, the Blackened Claw symbol was a standard of hobgoblin tribe.

Kenzo: So, so, Wellby, so based on what you seen, then, it feels like in this kind of period of kind of chaos after the Great War, after the dwarves abandon this keep, it seems that hobgoblins used this as some kind of a base for some period of time. But then something caused them to abandon it. Well, here’s a question for everybody. I mean, other than the folks that we just saw, is this place still occupied?
Delwath: There’s something in the keep, right.
after: Kenzo: I wonder if it’s you know this view that you have of the keep—Wellby you know, we’re here to learn, you know, we’re here to understand what’s going on. I wonder if it’s worth spending some time in that keep than just watching for a while, and just see what’s happening. Because what are they doing with those dogs? Are they transforming them? Are they amassing an army? Like, what’s—I wonder if it may be worth it for us to spend some time just observing this valley for a little bit. Actually, a meta-game: are we under time pressure to [garbled] like are we trying to get back at a certain time?
Delwath: We did have it, but it was weeks. I mean, it was on the order of weeks, not—
Seeker: Oh, and there are horses waiting as usual. Right, right.
DM: But so far, we’ve only it’s only been like six hours that you’ve—

Kenzo: Been. Right, right. Travel—so yeah, Wellby I wonder, you know, this view that you have of the keep—because if we’re under the valley right now, you know, if we keep traveling through this tunnel, we’re going to end up in Raven’s Hold probably at some point. And it’s feels like we don’t know what we’re up against, what we’re seeing. And I don’t know, it feels like maybe we—you found a spot where we can get some more intelligence, where we can learn more about the movements of these creatures and just studied for a while.

interactions.title: The iron guardian and lost dwarven craft
lines: Wellby: ((Earlier reconnaissance concerns))Speaking of which, the other thing that may be interesting to take a look down there is there’s this mechanical iron man that keeps walking back and forth down one of the side branches.
DM: Kenzo, this is not side branches down this tunnel, back in that—
Delwath: So wait, there’s a mechanical iron man patrolling the dwarven stronghold?
Wellby: Yes. Okay, kind of buried the lede.
Delwath: Okay, so doesn’t that mean hanging out watching through the windows sounds a little dangerous?
Wellby: Yeah, I mean, there’s a barrier of like rubble and stuff.
Delwath: Did the mechanical iron man have weapons?
Seeker: Wow, that’s an unusual sight. Have I heard about anything like this in the dwarven tradition?
Delwath: Yeah. Any—would this be—is there any magical animated iron creatures that I would have heard of?

DM: Seeker know something. Um, so yes, you have—this is this is a knowledge that is not—so you haven’t seen one of these things, but there are stories of of lost dwarven knowledge, of constructs powered by runes used to guard particularly important strongholds. So, your understanding is the secret of making them is not—has been lost.
DM: This thing has been around for hundreds of years, that could be. Not having seen it, it’s a little bit hard to tell anymore but—
Seeker: Right. There’s no reason to think that it would see us as threats to it. I—my question is: how would that thing behave?
Wellby: So I assume that it’s how the hobgoblins did this, because I assume this barrier barrier of rubble and such was something that they put up.
Seeker: Oh, to fence it in.
Seeker: They couldn’t destroy it; they could only sort of like make a barrier for it. Wow, that’s one—

before: Delwath: Or any of you geologist people able to guess where we might be that a passage going south west would make sense?
Seeker: Well…

Kenzo: My suggestion is just that maybe we split up right now at a couple of us, just for the remainder of the day, as long as there’s light, kind of try to keep an eye on what’s going on in the valley. And then a few of us can continue to map out and understand what’s going on with these tunnels very quietly, very cautiously, not making—not trying to attract attention to ourselves, and you know better sense of the lay of the land. We can reconvene in a few hours and, and then, you know, because I just—I’m just—you know, I hate caves. I hate caves. I don’t like where we are. I don’t like this place that we’re going to. This whole thing is not—it makes me really uneasy. I don’t want us emerging through some tunnel into who knows what the hell, what, um, I don’t know, it feels like it just—
Seeker: Comes out.

Kenzo: About these tunnels under here, be cautious about it. And then, you know, a couple of us can just keep an eye on the valley and who is moving around. Just get a better picture, because I hate bats. I’m like, I just—I mean, this whole thing and I’m just—I miss being in a city. This is—this whole situation is just not… Anyways, I’m just—I’m not at ease here.
after: Kenzo: Who’s the “They”.
Riswynn: [garbled], are you in—
DM: Are you in the small room with the rope leading up? Are you in the big cave right now?
Seeker: I think we must have all come up to the big cave because Riswynn didn’t come down or anything.
Delwath: Yeah, let’s—we’re all in the big cave.

But you don’t find anything else.

after: Kenzo: Yep.

DM: [garbled]. Okay, so you you push open the door, and you you come into here. Um a let’s let me see. I have too many windows open here. Ah, OK, so, um, this, this, again, is a fairly—it’s sort of an entry way room with similar to to the other room with with stairs going up and going down and you sort of come across into is basically a sort of a bare—a bare entry, and then there’s a door that leads to some other room on the other side of the door.

Dark cloak over its head. Um, carrying a scimitar—or sheathed on its back and moving sort of quietly and quickly from the floor above towards the living space.
DM: ((Combat resolution mechanics))he slumps down, and as he’s—as he’s slipping away, he says here, um, sort of muttering in his death, “Vengeance will be ours,” and he collapses.

interactions.title: Kenzo discovers, frees, and aids Vola
lines: DM: Ah, sure, you sort of like move over here and just kind of, peek in((Stealth mechanics))being very careful to avoid the two other creatures—creatures—and you see, lying on this pile of straw, um, a badly wounded woman wearing armor but otherwise um, like seemingly beat up, with no equipment or anything. Um, hands tied behind her back.
Kenzo: Um, are these other two, where are the other two dudes, or did they leave, or they still nearby?

DM: One of them left to head down the stairs on the other is like you know, walks over and sort of like gives her a kick. Muttering something, and says, “There will be more in the morning,” in common. And then heads out of the room and heads down the stairs.
Kenzo: The humanoid, right? Yeah, okay. Okay. All right. All right. Fuck.
DM: Alone in the room with her.
Kenzo: Yeah, I’m going to kind of get close, close-ish and then just whisper in Common, “But don’t be afraid. I’m here to help. Don’t make any noise.”
DM: So, um, this woman like startles and then seems to control her reaction, and you just hear a brief like mutter under her breath, “Holy fuck,” and looks like she’s looking around.
DM: Are you—she’s whispering, “What the bloody hell? What is going on?”
Kenzo: Your guess is as good as mine. I don’t know. I think I’m a friend. Well, my name is—I’m Kenzo. What’s your name?

Kenzo: Vola, I have a feeling that whatever those beasts are, they’re not your friend. They’re not my friend, either. I don’t know if that automatic automatically makes us friends, but I feel like it’s probably best for me to try to help you get out of the situation.
DM: I can’t argue with that.
Kenzo: Are they gonna come back? Are they done for the night, you know, they’re coming back up here?
DM: Probably not for several hours at least.
Kenzo: Okay, um, she, she bound?
DM: Her hands are tied. Yeah, okay.
Kenzo: I’m going to untie you, okay? I untie her.
DM: She like shakes her hands, like, rubs her wrists.

Kenzo: Okay, I have—I’m with friends. There—we are—we’re in the other tower. I’m going to figure out where—we are not trying to be detected by whatever the hell is going on here, and we need to talk to you to understand what’s going on about this place. It’s very important that we understand what’s going on here. But I’m going to try to help you get you out of this situation. So do you know if they’re if they’re leaving this whole tower? Are they are they still downstairs? Do you know if they stay down here?
DM: I think they will stay. What do I know? Been tied up in the damn prison.
Kenzo: How long you been here?
DM: I’ve lost track of days. It’s been some time, though.
DM: Not months, for sure. Not months.
Kenzo: How’d you get here? Oh.
DM: A week. How did you get here?

Kenzo: I’ll explain. I’ll explain. But my friends and I were trying to figure out what the hell is going on here, because whatever’s going on here is not right and we need to get down to the bottom of this.
DM: Who are your friends? Are you—did the Society send more people? Which society? I have not met you before. I don’t think I’ve met you before.
Kenzo: ((Abandoned Insight check))But all right, on the Society. What’s the Society?
DM: Perhaps we should find some other place to talk.
Kenzo: I agree. Let’s get you out of here. Stay here. Don’t make any noise to try to call attention. I’m going to go down and see if I can figure out a way to sneak us out of here, okay?
Kenzo: All right, just hang tight.
DM: Can you do that invisibility trick?

Kenzo: Um, not for you, but I don’t have a lot of time. So let me just scout downstairs and just see what’s going on. Stay here. Don’t make any noise to alarm them. I’ll be back in a minute, okay? Just stay right here. Tim, I go back down the stairs. I sneak down the stairs. Well, the orcs—are they, are they like—or the humanoids, where are they?
DM: So the orc has gone into the chambers. One of the humanoids is like sitting has pulled up a stool and is sitting by the stairs. The other has probably gone on into the chamber. You don’t see it.

Kenzo: ((Initial tactical discussion))I sneak back up, um, Vola, your name’s Vola. Vola, Vola, Vola. Excuse me. Sorry, Vola. Okay, look, I can’t attack these guys. As soon as I do, I’m going to become visible again. It’s going to cause a lot of attention. But, my friends—there’s—I’ve got four. I’ve got four companions with me. I think we can take these guards out quietly, okay?

So I’m going to go sneak back and get them. There, in the other tower, very, very close. Sit tight. Whatever you do, do not move. Do not cause alarm. We’re going to kill the guard as quickly, as quietly as we can, and then we’ll, we’ll come back and got you, okay? Can you hang—can you just hang here? And by the way, is she looks like she’s like wounded and beaten and stuff, right?
DM: She is. She looks like sick and nearly dead, yes.
Kenzo: Oh wow, okay. And look here, drink this.((Potion-equivalence mechanics))
Kenzo: I give her a healing potion. Drink this, rest. I’ll be back. We’ll be back in we’ll kill some guards, and we’ll get you out here, okay?
DM: She drinks it. She says, “Thank you. God, that goes down well. Yeah, I will.”
Kenzo: Just wait. We’ll be back.

before: Kenzo: It didn’t live there, that—

DM: The orc definitely seemed like it was heading towards its home—well, quarter’s, home, town—but a place where it’s staying. These two creatures seem like—I mean, you hear like moans and sort of groans coming from one of these here. I’m gonna have a map of this, so—

DM: Um, so you should have sort of moans coming from somewhere in here. It’s all done. Oh, right.

Kenzo: Let’s do this fast. I’m trying to get back to the crew. I just want to, like, it’s like, but figure out, like, you know, oh, here we go. Geez. Nice. So the moaning—is that, is that—can I go to the room where the moaning is coming from?

interactions.title: Vola’s mission, Agata’s relic hunt, and a possible alliance
lines: Kenzo: ((Session wrap-up))Um, so Vola, I know this is this is all—we don’t know who you are, and this whole situation is crazy to us. We’re here trying to figure out information ourselves, but these are the companions. Um, and if you guys want to introduce yourself. Or I can do it for you.

Riswynn: We’re not keen on poisoned water sources or.
